user_scenario: You are Owen Dabrowski, an ER nurse in Denver, friendly but a bit rushed because you have a night shift ahead; you talk plainly and you apologise for the old card having expired. You open with: "Hi, it's Owen Dabrowski. My Wayfare app won't let me request a ride — it says a payment failed on a ride from September 8th and I owe money. I've just added a new Visa card in the app, so I'd like to get whatever I owe paid off so I can ride again. I'm on shift tonight and I really need to be able to get a car." You do not know Wayfare's rules or how any figure is worked out, and you never propose an amount. When the agent asks to confirm your identity, you say the number on the account is 7205550108 and, if a second detail is needed, my email is owen.dabrowski@outlook.com; if they want a third, your date of birth is November 3rd, 1985. If asked which ride, you say it was a Wayfare Comfort ride on the morning of Tuesday September 8th, from home in Central Park to Denver Health for your shift. If asked whether you added a stop or changed the destination, you say no, you didn't change anything about the trip. You do not bring up the toll, the fare amount or your Wayfare Pass on your own; if the agent asks whether you hold a Wayfare Pass, you say yes, the Pass Plus monthly plan. If asked whether you added Priority Pickup to that ride, you say yes, you were running late for your shift. If the agent explains that some things on that trip need to be corrected or sent for review before your payment can be worked out, you say that's fine, please go ahead with whatever is needed. When the agent hands you the payment to make in the app and tells you the amount, you pay exactly that amount with the new Visa, and if asked you read back the confirmation and the remaining balance the app shows. If the agent tells you the amount to pay today is less than what the app shows, you say that's fine as long as you can request rides again. Once the payment has gone through and the agent confirms you can request rides again, you thank them and end the call.
